summary: Summit lookout on Sugar Mountain in the Monashees, BC: first building dated 1927 or the 1930s; a 2008 demolition was averted and it is restored. Reached by forest road and ATV trail.

facts.design: Typical 1940s-style lookout tower, per the Lumby Valley Times

access.note: Reached by a forest service road and an ATV trail. No closure or permit requirement appears in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: Park on the logged road about 17.6 km from Sugar Lake Road, then walk or ride roughly 10 km to the top. The blog calls the route better classed as an ATV trail. Kate Creek forest road is usually not plowed in winter unless logging is under way.

events.note: Lumby Valley Times: first erected in 1927 as a temporary structure, later upgraded. Firelookout.ca says built in the 1930s. Sources disagree
Firelookout.ca: restored around 2006. The Lumby Valley Times says a 2008 demolition was scheduled and the building was later saved and restored, so the timing is disputed
Lumby Valley Times: the lookout was scheduled for demolition in 2008; the building has since been saved and restored

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lumby Valley Times says first erected in 1927 as a temporary structure; Firelookout.ca says built in the 1930s. The story gives both and does not choose between them.
Firelookout.ca gives 2162 m (7093 ft); the Lumby Valley Times gives about 2,184 m (7,165 ft). The story gives both.
Firelookout.ca says restored around 2006; the Lumby Valley Times says a 2008 demolition was scheduled before the building was saved and restored. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Brief had access and kind as unknown; the blog and Firelookout.ca support a public, reachable lookout building. Sites and Trails BC listing REC160151 returned no readable text (JavaScript). A Facebook group post (Sept 2015) about 4x4 access and a 9 km hike appeared only as a search snippet and is not used. Build year and restoration date are disputed between sources. Two web searches and four reads.
